acceptance_criteria_verdicts.ac: AC1 — Full-viewport Leaflet map renders on /map
acceptance_criteria_verdicts.evidence: Screenshot ht008-map-after-latest.png: Leaflet zoom controls (+/-) and CARTO dark-tile attribution are visible, confirming Leaflet 1.9.4 initialized successfully. The map canvas element is visible and correctly overlaid by the app_shell. However, map tile images are not loading — the tile canvas area renders as solid black. CARTO CDN tiles (basemaps.cartocdn.com) appear unreachable or slow in the test environment. This is an environmental issue (CDN blocked/no internet), not a code defect, but it means no usable map surface is visible to the user.

acceptance_criteria_verdicts.ac: AC2 — Marker at each geo location with tooltip (name + device count)
acceptance_criteria_verdicts.evidence: No markers are visible in existing screenshots. Unable to determine if this is because (a) no geo location test data exists, (b) markers are present but invisible against the black tile background, or (c) marker rendering has a code defect. Code path in map_view.py _MAP_BRIDGE_JS marker creation loop is syntactically correct and uses standard Leaflet API. Integration test test_include_devices_returns_geo_map_payload confirms the API data contract (id, name, lat, lng, device_count, devices[]) is correct.

acceptance_criteria_verdicts.ac: AC3 — Cluster at low zoom (requires >10 close locations)
acceptance_criteria_verdicts.evidence: No test data with >10 close geo locations available. Interactive browser required to zoom and observe clustering. MarkerCluster plugin load is confirmed in map_view.py inject_map_view_assets(). Code confirms L.markerClusterGroup({maxClusterRadius:48}) is used and htRenderMap returns {ok:false, error:'cluster-plugin-unavailable'} if the plugin is missing.

acceptance_criteria_verdicts.ac: AC4 — Marker click opens right-side drawer with location name + device list
acceptance_criteria_verdicts.evidence: Code path confirmed correct: marker.on('click') fires emitEvent('map_location_selected', {location_id}), Python _on_map_location_selected handler calls _render_drawer(location) and sets drawer.set_visibility(True). emitEvent is a NiceGUI-provided global. The drawer element has correct positioning CSS (position:absolute; right:0; z-index:500). BUG-002 concerns the drawer open/close CSS: drawer visibility is toggled via NiceGUI set_visibility() which adds/removes display:none — but the drawer also has a CSS transition on transform (translateX). If NiceGUI set_visibility hides the element before the CSS transition finishes, the slide-in animation would be skipped. Cannot confirm without live interaction.

acceptance_criteria_verdicts.ac: AC5 — Device click in drawer navigates to topology with device pre-selected
acceptance_criteria_verdicts.evidence: Code path confirmed: device row button on_click calls ui.navigate.to(f'/topology?device_id={did}'). Implementation assumes the topology page honors the device_id query param for pre-selection. This is a HT-003 follow-up dependency noted in the HT-008 story spec. Cannot verify live.

acceptance_criteria_verdicts.ac: AC6 — Empty state text when zero geo locations
acceptance_criteria_verdicts.verdict: CANNOT DIRECTLY VERIFY (no empty-state test data)
acceptance_criteria_verdicts.evidence: Both screenshots show the map in 'ready' state (map canvas visible, Leaflet initialized), which means geo_locations was not empty when those screenshots were taken. Empty state code path is present: _set_state('empty') shows empty_card with _EMPTY_STATE_TEXT = 'No geographic locations yet — add a location with coordinates in Settings → Locations'. Text exactly matches the AC requirement. Cannot verify live render.

acceptance_criteria_verdicts.ac: AC7 — Dark tile variant in dark mode, WCAG contrast on controls
acceptance_criteria_verdicts.evidence: Code confirms use_dark_tiles = (theme_name != 'light') and tile_url uses _OSM_DARK_TILE (CARTO dark_all). CARTO attribution is visible in screenshots, confirming the dark tile URL is set. CSS overrides in _MAP_STYLE use design tokens (--ht-bg-surface-raised, --ht-text-primary, --ht-accent) ensuring zoom controls and attribution use themed colors. Actual WCAG contrast ratio cannot be measured without tiles rendering.

acceptance_criteria_verdicts.ac: AC8 — View resets to fit-all-markers on page reload (pan/zoom not persisted)
acceptance_criteria_verdicts.evidence: Code confirms: on every map_page() load, htRenderMap is called with a fresh fit to all marker bounds via map.fitBounds(points, {padding:[28,28]}). No pan/zoom state is persisted between renders. Logic is stateless — page reload reinvokes the full bootstrap path.

acceptance_criteria_verdicts.ac: AC9 — Fallback table when Leaflet fails to load
acceptance_criteria_verdicts.evidence: Code path confirmed: htRenderMap returns {ok:false, error:'leaflet-unavailable'} if window.L is missing. Python handler then populates fallback_table with all geo locations as rows and sets state to 'fallback'. Cannot artificially trigger this path without modifying code (out of scope).

bugs.title: Map tile images not loading — canvas renders black
bugs.action: Navigate to /map as authenticated admin with geo locations in DB
bugs.steps_to_reproduce: 1. Login as admin. 2. Navigate to /map. 3. Observe map canvas area.
bugs.observed: Leaflet initializes (zoom controls, CARTO attribution visible), map canvas is displayed, but all tile image requests either fail or are not made. Map area shows as solid black (the CSS background-color: var(--ht-bg-base) showing through).
bugs.expected: CARTO dark tile images load and display the world map.
bugs.likely_root_cause: The CARTO CDN (basemaps.cartocdn.com) is either unreachable or rate-limited in the current test environment. No code defect — tile URL format is valid (_OSM_DARK_TILE includes {r} which Leaflet replaces with empty string for non-retina). This is an environmental/network issue but may affect any user without reliable CDN access.
bugs.note: The map IS initialized correctly. AC1 is partially satisfied — the framework renders, just no tiles.

bugs.title: Drawer CSS slide-in transition may be skipped on NiceGUI set_visibility toggle
bugs.action: Click a geo location marker on the map
bugs.steps_to_reproduce: 1. Navigate to /map with geo locations present. 2. Click a marker. 3. Observe whether the drawer slides in with animation or appears instantaneously.
bugs.observed: Cannot directly observe (tooling blocker). Code analysis: drawer visibility is controlled by drawer.set_visibility(True/False), which NiceGUI implements by toggling display:none. The CSS specifies 'transform: translateX(100%)' (hidden) and 'transform: translateX(0)' via .ht-map-drawer-open class (visible). The CSS transition fires on the 'transform' property. However, NiceGUI set_visibility controls 'display', not the CSS class. The .ht-map-drawer-open class is never actually applied or removed anywhere in map.py — only set_visibility() is used. The CSS transform transition therefore has no effect: the drawer either shows instantly (display:block without .ht-map-drawer-open → transform remains translateX(100%), drawer off-screen) or hides (display:none).
bugs.expected: Drawer slides in from the right with a smooth transition when a marker is clicked.
bugs.actual_code_defect: The .ht-map-drawer-open CSS class is defined in _MAP_STYLE but never toggled in the Python event handler. set_visibility(True) only adds 'display:block' styling — the drawer would appear in its translateX(100%) off-screen position, making it invisible even when 'visible'.
bugs.severity_rationale: If confirmed, this is a logic error that makes the drawer functionally invisible. Severity upgraded from Low to HIGH pending live verification.
